column1: # co_check_ids.tsv -- APPEND-ONLY ap_id registry for CO-CHECK sibling lots (SPEC-flag-lot-item-model §2.2).
# A shared getItemFlagId drives several ItemLotParam lots; each SIBLING lot (every family member
# except the primary -- the lot the original region_map.csv row was named after, the family's
# lowest) becomes its own co-firing check. Its ap_id comes from HERE, never from a positional
# index: `ap_id = BASE_AP + row index` renumbers on any insertion (gen_data.py "APPENDED, never
# inserted"), and even tail-appends shift when the appended set grows. Registry ids are allocated
# once, in the reserved COCHECK band (>= 7900000; the positional band tops out ~7775300), and are
# NEVER reused or re-derived. Delisting a co-check retires its row in place (comment it out with
# the reason) -- the id stays burned.
# gen_data.py reads this file and PROJECTS a co-check location for every row whose flag is in
# CO_CHECK_FLAGS (the allowlist beside ROW_ITEM_NAME_FIX's old slot); a regen that needs an id
# not present here must fail loudly, never invent one. Keys must exist in flag_lots.tsv.
# Seeded 2026-07-24 with the four hand-verified shared-flag families (allocation order = sorted
# (flag, table, lot) at seed time; later additions APPEND with the next free id):
#   400696 lot 106931 -> Prayer Room Key   (primary 106930 = Ash of War: Flame Skewer)
#   510440 lot  10441 -> Scadutree Fragment (primary 10440 = Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns)
#   510460 lot  10461 -> Messmer's Kindling (primary 10460 = Remembrance of the Impaler)
#   520160 lot  20161 -> Golden Seed        (primary 20160 = Redmane Knight Ogha ash)
# 2026-08-06: 197 lot 10181 -> Great Rune of the Unborn (primary 10180 = Remembrance of the Full
#   Moon Queen). Rennala. Added on the ruling that the game COUNTS this rune toward the Leyndell
#   wall (#427) -- flag 197 is inside the counted 190-199 band. Until now the sibling was unmodelled,
#   so check_lots blanked only the primary and every kill handed out a real vanilla rune on top of
#   the AP item (#426).
